m1-l1.summary: Set up Python 3, Git, VS Code, and a course virtual environment, connect a free AI assistant (GitHub Copilot Free or a local model through Ollama), and confirm each piece from the terminal.
m1-l1.module: Set up a safe agent workbench

m1-l2.title: Make a practice repo and review your assistant's first change
m1-l2.summary: Build a small Git repository with tested Python code and agent instructions, have your assistant add a function on a branch, and check its work with git diff and your own test run.

m1-l3.title: Work safely with assistants, keep a log, and get unstuck
m1-l3.summary: Adopt the five safety rules this course runs on, scan text for secrets before you paste it into a chat, recover from a bad agent run with Git, and set up accessibility and privacy options.

m2-l1.title: Autocomplete, chat, and agents, and how to scope a task for each
m2-l1.summary: Tell autocomplete, chat, and agents apart by what they can see and change, trace the model-tool-result loop that makes an agent, and write a task spec with a boundary, acceptance criteria, and a stopping rule.

m2-l2.title: Build an agent harness that checks its own finish line
m2-l2.summary: Write a small agent harness in Python with tools, a step limit, write-scope enforcement, and an acceptance check, then run it against three scripted models that behave well, cut corners, and never stop.

m2-l3.title: Practice: sort tasks, write specs, and harden the agent loop
m2-l3.summary: Decide which tool fits a request, turn vague requests into specs, write a spec linter, and make an agent loop survive bad tool calls, repeated actions, huge outputs, and a failed finish line.

m3-l1.title: Map a repository, verify the AI's claims, and critique its plan
m3-l1.summary: Have an AI map an unfamiliar repository, check each of its claims with git ls-files, git grep, and the tests, and review a proposed plan for scope, order, missing verification, and risky assumptions.

m3-l2.title: Build a plan checker that tests an AI's plan against the real repo
m3-l2.summary: Write plan_check.py, which asks a scripted model for a plan as JSON and checks every step against the repository's actual file list, the task's scope, protected folders, read-before-edit order, test runs, and risky actions.

m3-l3.title: Practice: check an AI's claims and pick apart its plans
m3-l3.summary: Verify call-site and safe-to-delete claims with search, catch invented paths in a repository map, critique written plans, extend the plan checker with a tests-first rule, and detect out-of-order and circular plan steps.

m4-l1.title: Read a diff like a reviewer and demand evidence that it works
m4-l1.summary: Read unified diffs hunk by hunk, check a change's shape before its lines, spot weakened tests and plausible-but-wrong fixes, and tell real verification evidence from a claim, with help from linters and type checkers.

m4-l2.title: Catch a plausible AI fix with tests written from the spec
m4-l2.summary: Review an agent's bug fix for split_bill, confirm its claim, then write acceptance tests from the spec, watch them expose the flaw, apply a correct fix, and record evidence anyone can reproduce.

m4-l3.title: Practice: review diffs, test suspicious fixes, and check the evidence
m4-l3.summary: Parse which files a diff touches, find weakened tests and silenced failures, write tests that expose a plausible float bug, judge agent evidence reports, write a review comment, and build a review gate that combines it all.

m5-l1.title: Tool schemas, argument validation, and how MCP connects agents to tools
m5-l1.summary: Write tool definitions in JSON Schema, reject bad arguments before they run, trace the tool-calling loop, and map how MCP hosts, clients, and servers divide the work.

m5-l2.title: Build a validated tool loop, then serve the same tools over MCP
m5-l2.summary: Build three read-only project tools with JSON Schema validation, drive them with a scripted model in a capped tool-calling loop, then package them as an MCP server and connect it to a real host.

m5-l3.title: Practice: tighten tool schemas, tame the loop, and route MCP calls
m5-l3.summary: Six exercises that narrow broad tools, turn validation failures into useful messages, stop runaway loops, return the right kind of MCP error, and route calls across two servers, plus a read-only database tool challenge.

m6-l1.title: Least privilege, path sandboxes, and human approval gates
m6-l1.summary: Shrink what an agent can reach to what the task needs, using command allowlists, a path sandbox that blocks ../ and symlink escapes, effect tiers for tools, and approval prompts a person can actually judge.

m6-l2.title: Build a permission gate with a scoped sandbox and an approval step
m6-l2.summary: Build the checkpoint every agent tool call must pass, with a policy written as data, path scopes, a never-touch list, a command allowlist, a scrubbed environment, and a human approval step bound to the exact call.

m6-l3.title: Practice: break path guards, police commands, and scope approvals
m6-l3.summary: Six exercises on classifying tools for a task, finding and fixing path-guard escapes, protecting secrets inside the sandbox, checking command flags, single-use approvals, and scrubbed environments, plus a policy test suite challenge.

m7-l1.title: Why agents obey poisoned files, and the lethal trifecta
m7-l1.summary: See a naive agent read a planted README and leak a deploy token, learn why a model can't tell instructions from data, and use the lethal trifecta and the Agents Rule of Two to spot a workflow that can be turned into a data thief.

m7-l2.title: Build an injection-resistant agent with a sandbox, an exfiltration check, and an audit log
m7-l2.summary: Build a gate that treats tool output as data, confines reads to a sandbox, blocks outbound calls that carry a secret, asks a human for the rest, and logs every decision, then send a compromised model through it and watch nothing leak.

m7-l3.title: Practice: redact secrets, pin dependencies, and catch a poisoned tool
m7-l3.summary: Six exercises on keeping secrets out of logs and prompts, catching an encoded exfiltration attempt, spotting typosquatted and unpinned dependencies, and finding hidden instructions in a tool description, plus a tamper-evident audit log challenge.

m8-l1.title: Capstone brief: design and threat-model a safe sandboxed coding agent
m8-l1.summary: Read the capstone requirements, pick one of four projects at a difficulty you can finish, plan it on a template, and write a threat model that names the untrusted inputs, the assets, and the control that stops each path to harm.
m8-l1.module: Capstone: a safe sandboxed coding agent

m8-l2.title: Build the safe agent in milestones from a starter that runs offline
m8-l2.summary: Assemble the capstone agent in five milestones from a working starter: scaffold a sandbox repo, define validated tools, build the gate, run the loop against a scripted model, and have the harness write an auditable report while the planted attack is blocked.

m8-l3.title: Red-team your agent, demo it, and grade it against the rubric
m8-l3.summary: Turn your threat model into a passing test suite of attacks and normal work, rehearse a short demo that shows one attack blocked, grade yourself against a rubric, and plan where to take agent security next.

m1-l1.title: Set up Python, the harness project, and an optional local model
m1-l1.summary: Install or confirm Python 3.10+, create the harness-lab project with its own virtual environment, and, if you want a real model, install Ollama and pull a small model that can call tools.
m1-l1.module: Set up the harness workbench

m1-l2.title: Write the model interface and prove your setup works
m1-l2.summary: Define the complete(messages, tools) contract, build a scripted model and a real client for any OpenAI-compatible API, test the client's translation code offline, and run a setup check with an optional live call.

m1-l3.title: Test offline, protect your keys, and get unstuck
m1-l3.summary: Pin the model contract down with unittest, set up Git so keys and raw traces never get committed, decide what data each model option sends where, set the harness's safety rules, and fix the errors this course produces most often.

m2-l1.title: How an agent runtime works: the loop, tools, and stop rules
m2-l1.summary: See why a bare agent loop crashes on a single typo, then learn what turns it into a runtime, from the observe, plan, act, and verify cycle and validated tool schemas to errors returned as observations, stop rules, and a context that grows every step.
m2-l1.module: Build the runtime loop and tools

m2-l2.title: Build the tool registry and the agent loop
m2-l2.summary: Write tools.py (schemas, argument validation, and a dispatcher that never raises), file tools locked to one workspace folder, and loop.py with stop rules and a verify step, then watch a scripted model recover from bad calls and a false claim of success.

m2-l3.title: Practice: validate arguments, clip output, trim history, and stop stuck runs
m2-l3.summary: Six exercises and a challenge that harden the runtime loop, from range and enum checks to output clipping, stuck detection, token budgets, history trimming that keeps calls and results together, and a message-order checker.

m3-l1.title: What a sandbox must stop, and what a subprocess can't
m3-l1.summary: Work out what model-written code can do to your machine, contain the accidents with a child process that has a timeout, a clean environment, and a process group, see the attacks a subprocess can't stop, and learn when to retry, how to back off, and how to make retries safe.

m3-l2.title: Build the sandbox runner and let the agent run its own tests
m3-l2.summary: Write sandbox.py (a child process with a time limit, file and CPU limits, an output cap, a clean environment, and process-group cleanup), attack it with hostile code, give the agent a run_tests tool, add retries with backoff, and finish with an agent that fixes a bug and proves it with tests.

m3-l3.title: Practice: back off politely, contain paths, strip secrets, and repair code
m3-l3.summary: Six exercises and a challenge on recovery and containment, covering Retry-After headers, what full jitter does on average, a path check with a classic prefix bug, an environment allowlist with a secret guard, a crash-safe idempotency ledger, a bounded repair loop, and retries with a deadline.

m4-l1.title: Traces you can audit and eval sets that hold still
m4-l1.summary: Learn what a complete trace records and why JSON Lines suits it, how replaying a trace reproduces a run for free, how to turn real runs into frozen, versioned eval cases, and when to grade with deterministic checks or a model-based judge.
m4-l1.module: Record traces and build evaluation data

m4-l2.title: Record traces, replay a run, and freeze an eval set
m4-l2.summary: Write tracing.py and a traced loop, record six agent runs as JSONL, summarize and chart them, replay a run to find what changed, turn the traces into a versioned eval file with deterministic checks and a judge, and run the whole eval with one command.

m4-l3.title: Practice: query traces, redact secrets, split eval sets, and check the judge
m4-l3.summary: Six exercises and a challenge on traces and eval data, covering error rates per tool, redaction before anything is written, latency percentiles, a regression test built from a bad run, a stable held-out split, a tool-order grader, and measuring a judge against human labels with Cohen's kappa.

m5-l1.title: Grade agents with hidden tests, judges, and error bars
m5-l1.summary: Score agent output with exact match, hidden unit tests, and a rubric judge, compute pass@k the unbiased way, and put bootstrap confidence intervals on every number you report.

m5-l2.title: Build an eval runner that a gaming agent can't fool
m5-l2.summary: Grade two scripted agents on a pinned task set, watch the one tuned on visible tests win, then rebuild the grader with hidden tests and a per-run secret and report pass@k, cost, and bootstrap intervals.

m5-l3.title: Practice: catch gaming, judge the judge, and decide with intervals
m5-l3.summary: Seven exercises on tolerant grading, stable held-out splits, judge injection, judge-versus-human agreement, the bias in naive pass@k, contamination, and paired decisions, plus a test-tampering detector.

m6-l1.title: Split work across routers, planners, workers, and reviewers
m6-l1.summary: Learn the main multi-agent patterns (routers, planner-worker-reviewer, structured handoffs, shared state versus messages) and how to tell when splitting work helps and when it only multiplies the bill.

m6-l2.title: Build a planner, workers, and reviewer pipeline
m6-l2.summary: Wire scripted planner, worker, and reviewer agents into a pipeline that validates the plan, briefs each worker with only what it needs, rejects edits outside a worker's files, sends failures back with a cap, and gates the result on tests.

m6-l3.title: Practice: routers, handoffs, schedules, and shared state
m6-l3.summary: Six exercises and a challenge on routing that ignores claims in the request, tuning a confidence threshold, strict handoff parsing, scheduling subtasks without file conflicts, compare-and-set retries, critical-path speedup, and stopping reviewer ping-pong.

m7-l1.title: Put budgets, approvals, and an audit trail around agent teams
m7-l1.summary: Give a whole agent team one shared budget, stop loops that exact-repeat checks miss, gate irreversible actions on approvals bound to the exact action, issue each agent its own narrow short-lived credential, and keep a hash-chained audit log and a release checklist.
m7-l1.module: Control loops, approvals, and secure delivery

m7-l2.title: Build a supervisor that stops, asks, and keeps receipts
m7-l2.summary: Wrap Module 2's agent loop in a supervisor that enforces a token and time budget, freezes edits once the checks pass, checks a per-agent credential, asks a person before pushing, rolls back runs that stop improving, and writes a hash-chained audit log.

m7-l3.title: Practice: cost caps, risk tiers, two-person approvals, and release gates
m7-l3.summary: Seven exercises and a challenge on dollar budgets across models, delegation cycles in a handoff log, argument-aware risk tiers, two-person approval, catching a truncated audit log, scanning diffs for secrets, a release gate, and all-or-nothing edits with rollback.

m8-l1.title: Plan a secure, evaluated agent team
m8-l1.summary: Choose a capstone project, draw the system with its trust boundaries, write a threat model with an attack test for every control, size the evaluation so its intervals mean something, and fill in a one-page plan with five milestones.
m8-l1.module: Capstone: a secure, evaluated agent team

m8-l2.title: Build the capstone in five milestones
m8-l2.summary: Start from a runnable walking skeleton (tasks and a strict grader, a baseline and a reviewed worker, a guard with credentials and an audit log, an attack suite, and a generated report), then grow each milestone to the full brief.

m8-l3.title: Attack, measure, and present your agent team
m8-l3.summary: Test the capstone in three layers, run the held-out set once and report it next to the dev results, generate a security report that includes what your controls miss, polish the project, give a five-minute demo, and grade it against the rubric.

m1-l1.title: Get Python 3 and IDLE onto your computer
m1-l1.summary: Install Python 3 and its IDLE editor on Windows, macOS, or a Chromebook, then prove the install works with one line of code.

m1-l2.title: Write, save, and run your first program in IDLE
m1-l2.summary: Open IDLE's editor, write a three-line program, save it as a .py file, run it with F5, and break it on purpose to meet your first error message.

m1-l3.title: How class runs, where your files go, and fixes for setup trouble
m1-l3.summary: Learn the weekly rhythm of the live class, build a tidy folder for your .py files, and fix the setup problems students hit most often.

m2-l1.title: Show text and numbers with print(), and leave notes in comments
m2-l1.summary: See how Python runs a program one line at a time, use print() to show text and numbers exactly how you want, and write comments that make code easy to read.

m2-l2.title: Code-along: print a poster for adoption day
m2-l2.summary: Build a printed poster for an animal shelter one section at a time, using print(), sep, end, string repetition, backslash escapes, and comments.

m2-l3.title: Practice: fix broken prints, draw a tree, and print a receipt
m2-l3.summary: Six print() exercises plus a challenge, from introducing yourself to repairing broken code, predicting comments, and printing a receipt that does its own math.

m3-l1.title: Remember values with variables, and ask questions with input()
m3-l1.summary: Store values in variables, tell strings, integers, floats, and Booleans apart, and read what the user types with input() and type conversion.

m3-l2.title: Code-along: a launch briefing that does its own fuel math
m3-l2.summary: Build a program that interviews a ship's commander, converts each answer to the right type, works out fuel and meals, and prints a personalized mission briefing.

m3-l3.title: Practice: trace variables, convert input, and split a bill
m3-l3.summary: Trace variables by hand, identify data types, convert user input, fix a quiet type bug, swap two variables, and build a bill splitter that handles money.

m4-l1.title: Make decisions with if, elif, and else
m4-l1.summary: Use arithmetic and comparison operators, make programs choose between paths with if, elif, and else, and combine conditions with and, or, and not.

m4-l2.title: Code-along: the roller coaster ticket booth
m4-l2.summary: Build a ticket booth that checks a rider's height, prices tickets by age, handles season passes, gives every third ride free, and unlocks a Fast Lane with combined conditions.

m4-l3.title: Practice: even numbers, leap years, and rock-paper-scissors
m4-l3.summary: Solve six decision problems, from even-or-odd and making change to leap years and a login check, then play rock-paper-scissors against the computer.

m5-l1.title: Repeat anything with for, range(), and while
m5-l1.summary: Make Python repeat work for you with for loops, range(), and while loops that know when to stop.

m5-l2.title: Code-along: build a Guess the Number game
m5-l2.summary: Build a number-guessing game step by step, using a while loop, a try counter, and a random secret number.

m5-l3.title: Practice: loop drills, from countdowns to a star pyramid
m5-l3.summary: Practice for loops, range(), counters, and while loops with six exercises that get harder as you go, plus a star-pyramid challenge.

m6-l1.title: Keep many values in one list: indexes, len(), and loops
m6-l1.summary: Store many values in one variable with a list, reach each item by its index, and use loops to read and update every item.

m6-l2.title: Code-along: build a To-Do List Manager
m6-l2.summary: Build a menu-driven to-do list app that adds, shows, and checks off tasks stored in a Python list.

m6-l3.title: Practice: list workouts, from receipts to a class vote
m6-l3.summary: Practice indexing, looping over, searching, and updating lists with six exercises that build in difficulty, plus a vote-counting challenge.

m7-l1.title: Write your own functions and read Python's error messages
m7-l1.summary: Package code into reusable functions with parameters and return values, and learn to read Python's error messages to find and fix bugs.

m7-l2.title: Code-along: build a Pizza Party Planner from small functions
m7-l2.summary: Build a pizza-ordering calculator out of small functions, then find and fix a logic bug and a TypeError along the way.

m7-l3.title: Practice: write functions, then hunt down bugs
m7-l3.summary: Write functions that take parameters and return values, then hunt down syntax, name, type, and logic bugs in broken programs.

m8-l1.title: Capstone brief: pick a project and plan it on paper
m8-l1.summary: Read the capstone requirements, pick a text game, quiz, or tool you actually want to build, and plan it on paper before you write any code.

m8-l2.title: Capstone build: five milestones, a starter skeleton, and a worked example
m8-l2.summary: Build your capstone in five working milestones, starting from a skeleton file, and follow a complete Space Trivia quiz as it's built the same way.

m8-l3.title: Capstone finish: break it, fix it, polish it, present it
m8-l3.summary: Break your own program on purpose with a test table, write up a bug you fixed, polish the code, and get ready for your demo with the final checklist.

m1-l1.title: Install Android Studio and the Android SDK
m1-l1.summary: Check that your computer can run Android Studio, install it on Windows, macOS, Linux, or a Chromebook, and finish the setup wizard so the Android SDK is ready before Week 1.
m1-l1.module: Install Android Studio before class

m1-l2.title: Run Hello World on an emulator or your phone
m1-l2.summary: Create an Empty Views Activity project in Java, give it an emulator or a real phone to run on, and change one line to prove your whole setup works.

m1-l3.title: How class runs, and how to get unstuck
m1-l3.summary: Learn how the weekly live class runs, keep a tidy folder of projects, ask for help in a way that gets fast answers, and fix the Gradle, emulator, and memory problems that stop most first-time setups.

m2-l1.title: What's inside an Android project, and what Run does
m2-l1.summary: Walk the project tree file by file, from MainActivity.java and activity_main.xml to the manifest and the Gradle build files, and follow what happens between clicking Run and seeing your screen.
m2-l1.module: Tour an Android project and make it yours

m2-l2.title: Code-along: turn Hello World into your own app
m2-l2.summary: Create a fresh Java project, then give it your own name, a two-line greeting, and a color scheme through string and color resources, and run it on an emulator or phone.

m2-l3.title: Practice: find, change, and fix project files
m2-l3.summary: Six exercises that have you find answers in the project files, rename and version the app, add a footer, test on an old Android version, and repair a broken layout, plus a dark-mode challenge.

m3-l1.title: The Java you need for Android
m3-l1.summary: Learn the Java behind every Android app, from types, integer division, and strings to parsing input, methods, loops, classes, inheritance, and the lambdas that make buttons work, with programs that run right on the page.
m3-l1.module: Learn the Java that Android runs on

m3-l2.title: Code-along: a weekly habit tracker in Java
m3-l2.summary: Build a console habit tracker step by step, using a class with private fields, methods with conditions and loops, and an ArrayList of objects, the same shape as the code behind an Android list screen.

m3-l3.title: Practice: Java with types, strings, loops, and classes
m3-l3.summary: Solve six plain-Java exercises on number types, string rules, loops, safe parsing, classes with an ArrayList, and a listener lambda, then extend a class with inheritance in the challenge.

m4-l1.title: Build screens from views, layouts, and resources
m4-l1.summary: Arrange screens with LinearLayout and ConstraintLayout, use TextView, Button, ImageView, and EditText, size things in dp and sp, and keep text, colors, and sizes in resource files.

m4-l2.title: Code-along: a digital business card screen
m4-l2.summary: Build a polished business-card screen with a Material card, a vector avatar, contact details, a note field, and a button, using only resource-based strings, colors, and dimensions.

m4-l3.title: Practice: build layouts and fix broken ones
m4-l3.summary: Six layout exercises on resources, weights, constraints and bias, keyboards and autofill, image scaling, and views that only look right in the preview, plus a challenge that translates your business card into Spanish.

m5-l1.title: Make the screen react: taps, typed input, and surviving rotation
m5-l1.summary: Connect XML views to Java with findViewById, respond to taps, turn typed text into numbers without crashing, and keep your data when rotation rebuilds the Activity.
m5-l1.module: Make apps react to taps and typing

m5-l2.title: Code-along: a tip calculator that refuses bad input and survives rotation
m5-l2.summary: Build a tip calculator that reads a bill and a tip percent, answers bad input with a polite error instead of a crash, and keeps its result when the phone turns sideways.

m5-l3.title: Practice: counters, greetings, a converter, and the lifecycle detective
m5-l3.summary: Work through six exercises that connect views to code, validate typed input, and keep app state alive across rotation, then rebuild a counter on a ViewModel.

m6-l1.title: Scrolling lists with RecyclerView, and new screens with Intents
m6-l1.summary: Show a long scrolling list efficiently with RecyclerView and its adapter, then open a second screen and hand it data with an explicit Intent.

m6-l2.title: Code-along: Planet Facts, a list that opens a detail screen
m6-l2.summary: Build a two-screen app where tapping a planet in a scrolling RecyclerView opens a detail screen that receives the planet's data through Intent extras.

m6-l3.title: Practice: grids, recycling bugs, live updates, and sharing a fact
m6-l3.summary: Extend the Planet Facts app with a count header, a grid, recycling-safe highlights, runtime additions, and a share button, then delete rows with a long press as a challenge.

m7-l1.title: Remember data with SharedPreferences, find bugs with Logcat, and build an APK
m7-l1.summary: Keep small pieces of data after the app closes with SharedPreferences, track down bugs with Logcat, stack traces, and breakpoints, and build an APK you can install on any Android phone.
m7-l1.module: Save data, debug, and ship an APK

m7-l2.title: Code-along: a Quick Note app that remembers, and a bug to catch
m7-l2.summary: Build a one-screen note app that saves with SharedPreferences, hunt down a planted bug with Logcat and a breakpoint, and export the finished app as an APK.

m7-l3.title: Practice: saved settings, crash traces, a stepping bug, and a signed APK
m7-l3.summary: Save names, counts, and settings with SharedPreferences, read a real crash trace, step through a logic bug, produce a signed release APK, and save a whole list as a challenge.

m8-l1.title: Capstone brief: pick, plan, and sketch your own Android app
m8-l1.summary: Read the capstone requirements, choose an app idea that fits them, and plan its screens, data, and model class before writing any layout code.

m8-l2.title: Capstone build: five milestones from a working skeleton
m8-l2.summary: Build your capstone in five milestones, starting from a working two-screen skeleton with a RecyclerView list, an add and edit screen, saved data, and rotation-proof state.

m8-l3.title: Capstone finish: break it, polish it, present it
m8-l3.summary: Try to break your app with rotation, odd input, and background kills, polish what people will notice, then present it in a short demo graded against the rubric.

m1-l1.title: Get your computer ready and open the Scratch editor
m1-l1.summary: Check your computer, browser, and sound, choose how you'll open Scratch (no account, an account, or the app), and run a three-block test before the first class.
m1-l1.module: Get Scratch ready

m1-l2.title: Tour the editor, then make the cat introduce you
m1-l2.summary: Learn the five areas of the Scratch editor, then build "Meet Me", a short project where the cat slides in, tells everyone about you, flips, and meows.

m1-l3.title: Save your work, find it again, and get unstuck fast
m1-l3.summary: Learn the weekly class routine, save and reopen Scratch projects with or without an account, keep your files organized, and fix the problems that come up most in class.

m2-l1.title: Move sprites with x and y, and change how they look
m2-l1.summary: Read the stage like a map with x and y, move and glide sprites to exact spots, and change their look with costumes, backdrops, sizes, and effects.
m2-l1.module: Move sprites and change their looks

m2-l2.title: Code-along: Send the cat on a trip to space
m2-l2.summary: Build a two-scene animated story where the cat walks into a park, blasts off out the top of the stage, and floats among the stars, using coordinates, costumes, backdrops, and Looks effects.

m2-l3.title: Practice: corner tours, frog hops, and a balloon that pops
m2-l3.summary: Solve six challenges with coordinates, gliding, costumes, sizes, effects, and backdrops, then time a conversation between two sprites.

m3-l1.title: Make sprites react with events, repeat with loops, and play sounds on time
m3-l1.summary: Start scripts with the green flag, keys, clicks, and backdrop changes, repeat actions with repeat and forever loops, and choose the right sound block for the timing you want.
m3-l1.module: Animate with events, loops, and sound

m3-l2.title: Code-along: Throw a keyboard dance party
m3-l2.summary: Build a dance party where music loops, the lights flash, and you're the DJ, making the dancer slide, jump, pulse, and sing with keys and clicks.

m3-l3.title: Practice: arrow keys, flapping bats, and a metronome
m3-l3.summary: Solve six challenges with key, click, stage, and backdrop events, repeat and forever loops, and sounds, then build a fish tank with two loops running at once.

m4-l1.title: Make sprites decide with if, sense the world, and detect collisions
m4-l1.summary: Ask yes-or-no questions with Sensing and Operators blocks, make choices with if/then and if/else, move smoothly with key pressed?, ask the player questions, and detect when sprites touch each other, colors, or the edge.

m4-l2.title: Code-along: Build a maze game with solid walls
m4-l2.summary: Paint a maze, steer a player through it with the arrow keys, make the walls solid with color sensing, send escapees back to the start, and win by reaching a goal that cheers you on.

m4-l3.title: Practice: glow buttons, lava floors, and paddle ball
m4-l3.summary: Solve six challenges with if/then, if/else, ask and answer, invisible fences, color and sprite collisions, and a bug hunt, then build a paddle-and-ball game.

m5-l1.title: Notes: Keep score with variables and send messages with broadcasts
m5-l1.summary: Use variables to count score, lives, and time, and use broadcast messages so one sprite can tell every other sprite what just happened.

m5-l2.title: Code-along: Build Apple Catcher with score, lives, and a clock
m5-l2.summary: Build a catching game with a score, three lives, a 30-second countdown, and a game-over screen that every sprite reacts to.

m5-l3.title: Practice: Click counters, high scores, and a knock-knock joke
m5-l3.summary: Solve six challenges with variables, timers, and broadcasts, from a click counter to a knock-knock joke to a high score, then add a 3-2-1 countdown to Apple Catcher.

m6-l1.title: Notes: Fill the stage with clones and invent your own blocks
m6-l1.summary: Make many copies of one sprite while the game runs using clones, give each copy its own speed, and bundle repeated code into your own My Blocks.

m6-l2.title: Code-along: Space Shooter Waves with laser and rock clones
m6-l2.summary: Build a space shooter where a rocket fires laser clones at waves of falling rock clones, with My Blocks that spawn each wave and handle explosions.

m6-l3.title: Practice: Balloon pops, fish tanks, and runaway clones
m6-l3.summary: Practice making, placing, and deleting clones, build My Blocks with one and two inputs, fix a classic clone bug, and give every clone its own ID number.

m7-l1.title: Notes: Levels, clear endings, bug hunting, and sharing safely
m7-l1.summary: Add levels and clear win and lose endings to a game, watch a real player test it, find and fix bugs like a detective, and share or remix projects safely on Scratch.

m7-l2.title: Code-along: Maze Escape with two levels, lava, and lives
m7-l2.summary: Build a two-level maze game with walls you can't walk through, lava that costs a life, a goal star, and clear win and lose screens.

m7-l3.title: Practice: Level up Apple Catcher and hunt down four bugs
m7-l3.summary: Add level-ups and a win screen to Apple Catcher, track down four classic Scratch bugs, write a safe and honest project page, and record a best time in Maze Escape.

m8-l1.title: Capstone: Pitch and plan your own Scratch game
m8-l1.summary: Read the capstone brief, pick a game idea that fits the requirements, and plan it with a pitch, a requirement check, a storyboard, and a list of sprites, variables, and messages.

m8-l2.title: Capstone: Build your game one milestone at a time
m8-l2.summary: Build your capstone one working piece at a time, following a Meteor Dodge example that shows a skeleton, a player, clones and collisions, levels, and both endings.

m8-l3.title: Capstone: Playtest, polish, and present your game
m8-l3.summary: Test your capstone yourself and with a real player, make one fix from their feedback, save or share it safely, present it to the class, and check it against the rubric.

m1-l1.title: Open Colab and check your ML toolkit
m1-l1.summary: Set up Google Colab (or JupyterLab on your own computer), run your first cell, and confirm scikit-learn, pandas, numpy, and matplotlib are ready for Week 1.
m1-l1.module: Get your notebook ready

m1-l2.title: Load, plot, and score the wine data in your first notebook
m1-l2.summary: Run the full path you'll use every week (load a dataset, inspect it, chart it, train a model, score it) and prove your setup works end to end.

m1-l3.title: How class runs, and how to never lose a notebook
m1-l3.summary: Learn the weekly rhythm of the live class, keep notebooks organized and backed up in Drive, GitHub, or a downloaded .ipynb, and fix the setup problems students hit most often.

m2-l1.title: Honest test sets and the baseline to beat
m2-l1.summary: Walk through the supervised learning workflow, split data so the test set stays honest, stratify so the split is fair, and measure every model against a do-nothing baseline.

m2-l2.title: Code-along: rank five wine models against do-nothing baselines
m2-l2.summary: Build a reusable evaluation notebook that scores three dummy baselines and two real models on one stratified split, charts the leaderboard, and checks whether the ranking survives ten different splits.

m2-l3.title: Practice: splits, stratification, and baselines that fool you
m2-l3.summary: Predict baselines before computing them, see what stratify changes, catch a model that "never misses", compare regression baselines, expose an unfair comparison, and write a function that measures a model's gap over its baseline across many splits.

m3-l1.title: Clean, encode, and scale data without leaking the test set
m3-l1.summary: Fill in missing values with SimpleImputer, turn text categories into numbers with OneHotEncoder, scale features with StandardScaler, and chain them in a pipeline that learns only from training rows.

m3-l2.title: Code-along: rescue k-NN with a leak-free pipeline
m3-l2.summary: Take a messy version of the wine data with blanks and a text column, build one pipeline that imputes, encodes, and scales it, and watch k-NN jump from 64% to 98% without leaking test data.

m3-l3.title: Practice: imputers, encoders, and leak hunting
m3-l3.summary: Choose imputation strategies, predict one-hot output, fix a leaky script, build a full ColumnTransformer pipeline, test whether "this value was missing" is a clue, catch a feature that leaks the answer, and measure how leakage grows with noise.

m4-l1.title: Precision, recall, and the threshold that trades them
m4-l1.summary: Break a classifier's mistakes into a confusion matrix, measure them with precision, recall, and F1, move the decision threshold to trade false alarms for missed cases, and read precision-recall and ROC curves.

m4-l2.title: Code-along: pick a fraud-alert threshold the honest way
m4-l2.summary: Split data into train, validation, and test sets, build a threshold table and chart on validation data, choose the cutoff that meets a recall target, and confirm it once on the test set.

m4-l3.title: Practice: confusion matrices, positive classes, and the price of a mistake
m4-l3.summary: Compute precision, recall, and F1 by hand, catch the wrong-positive-class mistake, expose the accuracy paradox, move a threshold, read a three-class confusion matrix, compare models with PR curves, and choose the threshold that minimizes real-world cost.

m5-l1.title: Five scores beat one: cross-validation and learning curves
m5-l1.summary: Score a model on five different splits instead of one, report mean ± std, and read validation and learning curves to tell overfitting from underfitting.

m5-l2.title: Code-along: a validation report for a wine classifier
m5-l2.summary: Build a notebook that cross-validates a decision tree on the wine dataset against a baseline, picks its depth with a validation curve, checks a learning curve, and opens the test set exactly once.

m5-l3.title: Practice: cross-validation and diagnosing fit
m5-l3.summary: Work through six exercises on fold counts, sorted data, multi-metric scoring, validation curves for C and k, and learning-curve diagnosis, then build a reusable cross-validation report.

m6-l1.title: Compare models fairly, then tune them with grid and random search
m6-l1.summary: Compare a decision tree, a random forest, and logistic regression on identical folds, tune hyperparameters with GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV, and see why the winning CV score is slightly too good.

m6-l2.title: Code-along: a tuned model shootout on handwritten digits
m6-l2.summary: Tune a decision tree, a logistic regression, and a random forest on the same folds, rank them on a leaderboard with error bars, open the test set once for the winner, and look at the digits it still gets wrong.

m6-l3.title: Practice: fair comparisons and hyperparameter search
m6-l3.summary: Fix pipeline parameter names, budget a grid before running it, compare models on paired folds, tune a preprocessing step, sample C on a log scale, rescue a search whose best value sits on the edge, and compare two tuned models with nested cross-validation.

m7-l1.title: Rare classes, hidden failures, and the one-page model report
m7-l1.summary: See why accuracy collapses on imbalanced data, compare class weights with a deliberately chosen threshold, find where a model fails by slicing its errors, and write it all up in a one-page report.

m7-l2.title: Code-along: a screening model that rarely misses
m7-l2.summary: Build a breast-tumor screening model with a 99% recall target, test whether class weights help, choose the threshold from out-of-fold predictions, slice its false alarms, check the test set once, and print a report generated from the results.

m7-l3.title: Practice: imbalance, slices, and limitations
m7-l3.summary: Expose the accuracy trap, test class weights on a tree, pick thresholds from a precision requirement and from error costs, slice a model's errors, write a specific limitations paragraph, and evaluate threshold tuning without leaks.

m8-l1.title: Capstone brief: a model evaluation report someone could act on
m8-l1.summary: Understand the capstone requirements, choose a dataset and the decision your model supports, estimate your compute budget, and write a one-page plan before you train anything.

m8-l2.title: Capstone build: eight milestones and a starter notebook
m8-l2.summary: Build the capstone in eight checkable milestones using a starter notebook that runs end to end on the breast cancer data, swapping in your own dataset, metric, threshold rule, and slice feature as you go.

m8-l3.title: Capstone finish: sanity checks, a sharper report, and a five-minute talk
m8-l3.summary: Run four sanity checks that catch leaks and fragile results, tighten your one-page report, rehearse a five-minute presentation, and grade your own work against the rubric.
